title: Shark Emoji 🦈 Meaning: Predators, Baby Shark and More
description: The 🦈 shark emoji means the ocean’s top predator, ruthless ambition, Shark Week and Baby Shark. Find out how it is used in business, gaming, fandoms and texts.
summary: The 🦈 shark emoji represents sharks and the fear and fascination around them. Figuratively it describes a ruthless competitor, such as a loan shark, pool shark or aggressive dealmaker. It also points to Shark Week, the children’s song Baby Shark, the San Jose Sharks and IKEA’s plush shark, Blåhaj.
meaning: Start with the animal. 🦈 goes on beach photos with a nervous joke, on aquarium trips, on diving posts and on every summer rewatch of Jaws. Each July and August it spikes with Shark Week, the long-running Discovery Channel event. For parents of small children it means one thing only: Baby Shark, the song whose video became one of the most-watched on YouTube and which is usually typed with a resigned “doo doo doo.”

Applied to people, a shark is someone who hunts. English has loan sharks who lend at brutal rates, card and pool sharks who hide their skill to take your money, and lawyers and negotiators praised or feared as sharks. The investors on the television show Shark Tank lean into the label. So the emoji can be a compliment on someone’s killer instinct in business or sports, or a warning that a person is circling for advantage.

Two communities have given the emoji friendlier meanings. Hockey fans use it for the San Jose Sharks. And IKEA’s large blue plush shark, Blåhaj, became an internet favorite and an informal mascot among transgender people online, so 🦈 appears in trans and queer spaces as an affectionate in-joke, often beside the trans flag. In gaming, “sharking” can mean preying on weaker players, and the emoji labels that too.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends use it for ocean jokes before a beach day, for someone who eats fast or pounces on the last slice, and for anyone who smelled blood in an argument. “She’s a 🦈 in meetings” is admiration with a hint of caution. Parents send it with eye-rolling affection when the toddler demands the song again.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: In sales, finance, law and startups, calling a colleague a shark praises their aggressiveness in closing deals. It appears in pitch-competition posts that borrow the Shark Tank format. Use it knowingly, since the same word describes predatory lenders and people who exploit others, and not everyone hears it as praise.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Summer brings Shark Week memes, drone footage of sharks near swimmers and Jaws references. Year-round, Blåhaj content keeps the emoji busy: photos of the plush tucked into bed or sitting at a desk, frequently posted by trans creators. Under those posts 🦈 signals belonging, not danger.

examples.text: Not going past my knees, I’ve seen Jaws 🦈
examples.meaning: A joke about being afraid of sharks at the beach.
Praise for a ruthless, skilled negotiator.

examples.meaning: A tired parent whose child keeps playing the song.

examples.meaning: Warns that he is a pool shark who hustles opponents.
Celebrating the IKEA plush shark loved in trans communities.
Looking forward to the annual TV event.

combos.meaning: Sharks in the water; ocean wildlife or a beach warning.
A loan shark, or a dealmaker hungry for profit.
Smelling blood in the water; sensing weakness and moving in.

confusedWith.difference: 🐬 is a friendly, leaping marine mammal associated with playfulness, vacations and intelligence. A fin in the water could belong to either, but the emojis carry opposite moods: dolphins are fun, sharks are threatening or ruthless.

🐋 stands for enormous size and, in finance and gaming, a big spender or major holder. A whale is powerful through scale. A shark is powerful through aggression, and the terms are not interchangeable in business slang.
🐟 is a small generic fish for fishing, seafood and the saying about plenty of fish in the sea. In poker a “fish” is the weak player a shark feeds on, so the two are opposites at the table.

avoid: Avoid joking with it right after news of a real shark attack.
Do not call a client or boss a shark unless you know they take it as a compliment.
Skip it when recommending a lender or adviser, where “shark” implies exploitation.
design: The emoji shows a full-body gray or blue-gray shark with a pale underside, a tall dorsal fin and a pointed snout, usually swimming to the left. Apple’s resembles a great white with visible gills and teeth; Google’s is a smoother cartoon. Some versions show the mouth open, others closed. The designs agree on shape and color, so no platform changes the tone.

faqs.q: What does 🦈 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: It depends on the topic. About work or games, they are calling someone fierce and competitive. About the beach, it is a joke about danger. In queer and trans spaces it likely refers to the Blåhaj plush. It is not a flirting emoji.

faqs.q: Why is the shark emoji associated with trans people?
faqs.a: IKEA’s soft toy shark, Blåhaj, became widely loved in online trans communities, helped by its blue, pink and white coloring resembling the trans flag. Sharing photos of the plush became a tradition, and the emoji followed as shorthand.

faqs.q: What does it mean to call someone a shark?
faqs.a: It means they pursue what they want aggressively and are skilled at exploiting an opening. In business it can be admiring. In lending, gambling or dating it suggests the person preys on others, so tone and setting matter.

faqs.q: When was the shark emoji released?
faqs.a: It was added in 2016. Earlier keyboards had fish, whales and a dolphin but no shark, so Shark Week posts before then had to improvise with other sea creatures.
